chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to pick his teeth with everything he came across, except for the palm leaves and the reeds.

key_terms.الْخُوصَ: palm leaves / twigs of date palm
key_terms.يَتَخَلَّلُ: to pick teeth / use a toothpick

ai.seo_question: What materials did the Prophet use for cleaning his teeth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) practical adherence to the Sunnah of using the siwak (toothstick) with whatever natural material was accessible, emphasizing ease and flexibility in personal hygiene. By explicitly excluding palm leaves (khawis) and reeds (qasab), the narration clarifies that while the act of cleaning teeth is encouraged, the specific material is not rigidly prescribed, allowing for adaptation to local availability. This reflects the Shia scholarly view on the adaptability of prophetic practices to circumstantial needs while maintaining ritual purity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to pick teeth with everything he<sup>saww</sup> came across except for the palm leaves and the reeds’.
en.sarwar: It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from certain ones who narrated who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited using pomegranate fragments as toothpicks, as well as myrtle and reeds, saying that they stir up the erosive vein.’”
